protocol_manager-deposit.name: deposit
protocol_manager-deposit.description: Deposit tokens into a specified protocol. The function resolves the protocol plugin via the Beacon, verifies the plugin, forwards the token deposit from ProxyGeneral to the plugin, calls the plugin’s deposit function, and emits a ProtocolOperationExecuted event.
protocol_manager-deposit.signature: function deposit(string memory protocolName, string memory tokenCode, uint256 amount) external onlyOwner
protocol_manager-deposit.accessControl: external onlyOwner – callable exclusively by the contract owner.
validations: ✅ amount > 0 – enforced by if (amount == 0) revert InvalidAmount(amount);
✅ tokenCode non‑empty – enforced by if (bytes(tokenCode).length == 0) revert InvalidTokenCode(tokenCode);
✅ protocol plugin resolution – if the plugin address is 0, the contract reverts with ProtocolNotFound.
✅ plugin address non‑zero – checked by _validateProtocol() which reverts with InvalidProtocol if zero.
✅ plugin.deposit must return true – otherwise the function reverts with OperationFailed("deposit", "Plugin deposit failed").
protocol_manager-deposit.gasCost: ≈ 120,000–140,000 gas (cold storage reads, beacon lookup, low‑level plugin call, SafeERC20 withdrawal).
protocol_manager-deposit.usageExample:
// Example usage by the contract owner
protocolManager.deposit(
protocol_manager-deposit.calledBy: external caller – only the contract owner can execute this function.
securityNotes: ⚙️ Only the owner can call deposit; any other address is rejected by the onlyOwner modifier.
🔒 Sufficient checks prevent accidental zero‑amount deposits or empty token codes.
🛡️ The beacon lookup ensures the correct plugin contract is used; an invalid plugin triggers a revert.
🛠️ The function relies on the plugin’s deposit() returning true; failure leads to a revert to protect funds.
protocol_manager-deposit.notes: Part of the core module‑registration and proxy pattern that routes deposits through ProxyGeneral and the selected plugin.

protocol_manager-withdraw.name: withdraw
protocol_manager-withdraw.description: Withdraw tokens from a specified protocol. The function resolves the protocol plugin via the Beacon, verifies the plugin and then delegates the withdrawal to the plugin, which returns the tokens to ProxyGeneral. A ProtocolOperationExecuted event is emitted.
protocol_manager-withdraw.signature: function withdraw(string memory protocolName, string memory tokenCode, uint256 amount) external onlyOwner
protocol_manager-withdraw.accessControl: external onlyOwner – callable exclusively by the contract owner.
validations: ✅ amount > 0 – enforced by if (amount == 0) revert InvalidAmount(amount);
✅ tokenCode non‑empty – enforced by if (bytes(tokenCode).length == 0) revert InvalidTokenCode(tokenCode);
✅ protocol plugin resolution – reverts with ProtocolNotFound if plugin address is 0.
✅ plugin address non‑zero – _validateProtocol() reverts with InvalidProtocol.
✅ plugin.withdraw must return true – otherwise the transaction reverts with OperationFailed("withdraw", "Plugin withdraw failed").
protocol_manager-withdraw.gasCost: ≈ 110,000–130,000 gas (cold storage reads, beacon lookup, low‑level plugin call, SafeERC20 transfer).
protocol_manager-withdraw.usageExample:
// Example usage by the contract owner
protocolManager.withdraw(
protocol_manager-withdraw.calledBy: external caller – only the contract owner can execute this function.
securityNotes: ⚙️ Only the owner can call withdraw; unauthorized callers are rejected by the onlyOwner modifier.
🔒 Input validations prevent zero amount or empty token codes.
🛡️ The plugin is verified via the beacon and address checks, ensuring the token is returned to the correct proxy.
🛠️ A failed plugin return leads to a revert, protecting the caller from loss.
protocol_manager-withdraw.notes: Designed to route withdrawals through the plugin system and back to the ProtocolManager, emitting an event for auditability.
